description.narrative:
1. Problem Statement: What specific problem would you like to address? Whilst solar technology has been a game changer for improving the reliability of water pumping equipment and reducing the unity cost of supplying water, it has one obvious should coming, namely its reliant on the solar day. This becomes a hinderance for water schemes where pumping is required beyond the solar day i.e. early in the morning, late in the evening and during the nighttime. One of the most widely adopted mitigations to this is the use of diesel generators to provide for this prolonged pumping. These solutions are known as dual power systems where solar is used when the sun is shining, and generator is switched on when the sun’s energy is not sufficient to deliver water.Dual power systems are also necessary for short seasonal demand increases, or where the water source is constrained, to address storage constraints, as well as to reduce solar anxiety, particularly where confidence in the technology by user communities is low.
Traditionally, the switching of dual power systems is done manually, introducing inappropriate and inefficient use of the resources as water operators have to usetheir judgment in switching between solar and diesel. Site visits by Oxfam have found records of systems that run on generator evenwhen solar is sufficient to deliver the required water for that time, resulting in reduced cost benefits of the solar water pumpingsystem (SPWS).
2. Proposed Solution to the problem and why is it innovative?
Solar pumping equipment providers (Grundfos and Lorentz) have developed seamless power blending solutions that allow simultaneous supply of both DC power from solar and AC power from diesel generators (or grid) to the pump. Hybrid power operation allows a second power source to be connected which complements the solar power. The hybrid power blending inverter will prioritize solar and blend in the second power source, according to the pre-defined water and pressure need. This hybrid function significantly reduces energy costs resulting in lower operational costs from grid or generator. The hybrid inverters allow the pump to operate with solar only, to combine solar with grid or generator power by blending power sources, or to operate only with grid / generator, providing an automated choice of power based on the demand.
The inverter will give priority to the DC solar energy as the primary power source when it’s available and blends in the second power source (diesel/grid) when needed, ensuring the pump and motor operate at top performance. It provides for continuous power supply, continuousuninterrupted pumping, 24/7 if required. It is a fully automated arrangement (devoid of any human intervention), removing the riskto not only the equipment but also to the users which an important aspect in safe programming within Oxfam.
Although this is now acommercial technology, to our knowledge there is no example where this has been installed and the the performance monitored. OxfamUganda plans to install one unit at Sewswe water treatment plant in Kyaka camp to power a hybrid raw water pump which can currentlybe operated by solar, grid or diesel generated electricity. Blending of solar power with either grid or generator will maximise the use of available solar energy and stabilise the flow rate which will have the added benefit of simplifying the water treatment chemical dosing at the Sweswe clarifier.
Oxfam Uganda team and its partner Nsamizi are committed to monitor the performance ofthe system and share learning with the aim of demonstrating cost and energy savings and confirming the performance and reliability of the equipment.
The results of this activity will be documented and disseminated within the Oxfam WASH community to inform future adoptionand scale up in other schemes within Uganda and globally.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
